## Overview

MethScope is the R package interface for MRMP-based sparse methylome analysis.
For users who prefer a standalone command-line workflow, we also provide
**MethScope2**, a pure-C implementation:

<https://github.com/zhou-lab/MethScope2>

MethScope2 implements the main command-line path:

```text
query .cg + MRMP reference -> cell-by-pattern matrix -> prediction/deconvolution/upscaling
```

It uses YAME for `.cg/.cm` input/output and summary computation, and links
`libxgboost` for model inference. It does not require an R runtime.

## When to Use MethScope2

Use the R package when you want an interactive analysis workflow inside R,
including plotting, training, and integration with R objects.

Use MethScope2 when you want:

- command-line batch processing
- integration into shell/HPC workflows
- a no-R-runtime implementation
- direct CLI prediction, matrix generation, deconvolution, or upscaling

## Build MethScope2

MethScope2 depends on YAME, vendored as a git submodule, and `libxgboost` from
conda-forge.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Clone with the YAME submodule
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/zhou-lab/MethScope2.git
cd MethScope2

# Install libxgboost
conda create -n methscope2 -c conda-forge libxgboost
conda activate methscope2

# Build the CLI
make
```

If `libxgboost` is installed outside the active conda environment, pass its
prefix explicitly:

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
make XGB_PREFIX=/path/to/conda/env
```

The built binary is named `methscope2`.

## Example Commands

The exact model and fixture files are documented in the MethScope2 repository.
The commands below show the main usage pattern.

### Cell-Type Prediction

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
methscope2 predict query.cg model.ubjx > prediction.tsv
```

Here, `query.cg` is a YAME `.cg` file and `model.ubjx` is a bundled MethScope2
XGBoost classifier. Model bundles can carry their own MRMP reference, so users
do not need to pass a separate `.cm` file when using a self-contained bundle.

### Generate a Feature Matrix

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
methscope2 matrix query.cg model_or_mrmp > input_pattern.tsv
```

This generates a sample-by-MRMP feature matrix analogous to `GenerateInput()` in
the R package.

### Deconvolution

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
methscope2 deconv -p 1000 mixture.cg reference.refx > deconv.tsv
```

The `.refx` file is a MethScope2 deconvolution reference bundle. The `-p`
argument controls the number of MRMP patterns used.

### Upscaling

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
methscope2 upscale -o reconstructed.cg upscale_model.updecx sparse_input.cg
```

This reconstructs CpG-level methylation calls from sparse input using an
upscaling decoder bundle.

## Relationship to the R Package

The two implementations are intended to be complementary:

- **MethScope R package**: interactive R analysis, plotting, training,
  visualization, and R-based downstream workflows.
- **MethScope2 C CLI**: standalone command-line processing for production,
  batch, and HPC workflows.

For the complete MethScope2 build instructions, model bundle formats, and test
examples, see:

<https://github.com/zhou-lab/MethScope2>

## Notes on Input Order

MethScope2 emits one row per query record in query-file order. When supplying
labels for training or evaluation, make sure the labels follow the same query
record order. In the MethScope R package tutorial, the example labels follow the
`.cg.idx` sample order.
